description: Online team dreaming big about the Moon! Planning the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge: a web tool comparing landing sites and time windows, plus each site's resource potential (water ice, sunlight). Open to a game challenge too. We have front-end covered (HTML/CSS/JS). Looking for data analysis, lunar science, design or storytelling. Please commit time on Nov 14-15!
summary: We developed an html webpage. By inputting a time and a coordinate, it calculates the sunrise/sunset and earth-rise/earth-set on the moon. Because current missions are mainly based on solar power, so access to sunlight is important. Similarly, missions on the far side of the moon need relay to communicate with Earth. Especially at the moon's poles, where libration may affect direct communication with Earth. Therefore this project aims to act as a referencing point to these planning variables for future mission plannings.
details: By inputting a time and a coordinate, it calculates the sunrise/sunset and earthrise/earthset on the Moon. This project allows future mission planners to quickly plan based on their chosen sites. This way, when a mission plan changes due to unexpected delays, they can quickly adjust and avoid further delays. We hope this project can be used as a reference point for any future mission planning. We used HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript (no backend), Plotly.js to render the interactive 3D Moon globe, the open-source astronomy-engine library to compute the Sun and Earth positions and rise/set times, a lunar surface texture from Wikimedia Commons, and GitHub with GitHub Pages for version control and hosting. We used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI assistant for coding, debugging, and troubleshooting. It is a creative project as it is presented visually as a 3D interactive Moon. The project includes 13 past landing sites and 2 future Artemis landing sites and working time for the plans.
